name: EOG for Gaze Tracking
description: Captures horizontal eye movements using electrooculography for gaze-based control interfaces. Uses DC-coupled acquisition (no highpass filter) to preserve the slow corneoretinal potential that shifts with eye position. Delta modulation encoding at 5 uV threshold converts continuous gaze position into spike events representing eye movement direction and velocity.
electrode_placement:
## Horizontal EOG

1. **Clean skin** with alcohol wipe at the outer corners of both eyes
2. **Channel 0 (hEOG+):** Place electrode on the outer canthus (corner) of the right eye
3. **Channel 1 (hEOG-):** Place electrode on the outer canthus (corner) of the left eye
4. **Reference:** Place on the center of the forehead (Fpz)
5. **Ground:** Place on the mastoid bone behind the ear

**Verification:** Look left and right repeatedly. You should see a clear dipolar signal: positive deflection when looking right, negative when looking left. Signal amplitude should be 50-200 uV for a full lateral saccade.
